Data-protection rules under the GDPR apply to BB (Baseline Behavior; standard user behavior used for anomaly detection) telemetry and any personal data processing (Art. 4(5) pseudonymisation; Art. 5(1)(c),(e) minimisation/storage limitation; Art. 6(1)(a)/(f) lawful bases; Art. 8 child-consent; Art. 46 SCCs for transfers). Practical product implications requiring geo-specific logic: (1) GH (Geo-handler; a module responsible for routing features based on user region) must enforce EEA-only exposure at routing/delivery; (2) implement notice-and-action intake, triage, takedown, logging and redress workflows to support DSA reporting; (3) instrument telemetry/BB (Baseline Behavior; standard user behavior used for anomaly detection) to minimise personal data, pseudonymise where required, and permit opt-outs; (4) ensure retention and cross-border transfer controls (SCCs/art.46) and GDPR lawful-basis management (consent vs legitimate interest, age checks per Art.8); (5) prepare for VLOP-level obligations (systemic risk assessments, audits) if thresholds are met. GH (Geo-handler; a module responsible for routing features based on user region) (Geo-handler) will gate exposure by region; BB (Baseline Behavior; standard user behavior used for anomaly detection) (Baseline Behavior) will collect telemetry/analytics for anomaly detection and feedback.", "needs_geo_specific_logic": true, "reasoning": "Multiple Jury reports agree the feature is region-targeted (EEA per feature text) and combines hosting user-generated video content with telemetry, which triggers EU-specific obligations under the Digital Services Act (DSA) and personal-data obligations under the GDPR. Product-level geo-specific logic is required so GH (Geo-handler; a module responsible for routing features based on user region) can enforce EEA-only exposure and produce auditable logs proving regional gating. Operational implications include implementing DSA notice-and-action intake/triage/takedown/logging and internal complaint-handling and transparency reporting workflows (Articles 14–16, 15/24, 20), documenting recommender-system parameters and user controls if algorithmic surfacing is used (Article 27), and preparing for VLOP-level systemic risk assessments/audits if designation thresholds apply (Articles 33–37). BB (Baseline Behavior; standard user behavior used for anomaly detection) telemetry must be designed to comply with GDPR principles: data minimisation and storage limitation (Art.5(1)(c) & 5(1)(e)), pseudonymisation (Art.4(5)), lawful-basis selection and recording (Art.6(1)(a)/(f)), child-consent protections (Art.8), DPIA when high risk (Art.35), and cross-border transfer safeguards (Art.46(2)(c) / SCCs). Conflicts / open items: the feature text explicitly states EEA, but some metadata references 'EU' — this territorial-scope discrepancy should be resolved before rollout (GH (Geo-handler; a module responsible for routing features based on user region) config must reflect the confirmed scope). Also, the available document chunks are secondary summaries (wiki and guidance); legal should validate exact obligations and reporting formats against authoritative EUR-Lex/GDPR texts before
